home.safetyText: Simple steps based on National Disaster Management Authority guidance.
home.tips.before: Keep a torch, radio, spare batteries, medicines, drinking water and dry food ready.
Put important documents in a waterproof bag.
Charge your phone and know where your nearest cyclone shelter is.
Fishermen: do not go to sea. Secure boats and nets.
home.tips.during: Stay indoors and away from windows. Switch off electricity and gas.
Follow radio, TV and official SMS updates.
If your house is unsafe, move to a shelter early.
Do not go out when the wind suddenly calms — it can return from the other side.
home.tips.after: Wait for the official all-clear before going out.
Stay away from fallen power lines and damaged buildings.
Drink only boiled or purified water.
Report damage and injuries to local authorities.
home.helpText: Free to call from any phone in India.

home.how.d: ISRO's INSAT-3DS images the ocean every 30 minutes; NASA measures the rain.
Our model spots organised storm clouds over warm sea and measures cloud height and rainfall.
Storm positions and forecasts come from official warning centres; the AI adds early hints.
Plain safety advice in English and Hindi, for everyone on the coast.

impact.x.title: Impact assessment
impact.x.noActive: No official system is active. Exposure is computed automatically when one forms; past storms are below.
impact.x.methodItems: Population: GeoNames cities1000 (every town or city with at least 1,000 people, CC-BY 4.0). Villages are not included, so exposure is a lower bound.

Zones along the track (interpolated every 25 km): destructive core = within 60 km where wind ≥ 64 kt; strong-wind zone = within 150 / 200 / 250 km where wind ≥ 34 / 48 / 64 kt (typical North Indian Ocean radii, not storm-specific wind fields).
Upcoming storms use the current position plus the official forecast track (AI track if no official one).
Similar storms: recorded cyclones whose peak wind is within ±20 kt of the forecast peak. Deaths and damage are approximate published figures (see links).

storm.impact.methodText: People living inside each wind zone, from the GHS-POP 2020 population grid (~1 km), using the storm’s measured wind radii (JTWC) where available, otherwise typical radii for its strength. Figures show exposure — people within reach of those winds — not the number harmed. Storm-force exposure is closest to officially reported “people affected” (e.g. Phailin 2013: 1.08 crore vs 1.32 crore reported).
